chunks: Zur‘ah and ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Īsā narrated from Samā‘ah, who said:

I asked him about a man who digs a well in his house or on his land. He said: “As for what he digs in his own property, there is no liability upon him. But as for what he digs in the road or in other than his property, then he is liable for whatever falls into it.”

key_terms.الْبِئْرَ: a well that is dug into the ground
key_terms.ضَمَانٌ: legal liability or responsibility for resulting harm
key_terms.غَيْرِ مِلْكِهِ: property that does not belong to him
key_terms.مِلْكِهِ: his owned property or lawful possession

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if someone or something falls into a well he dug?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on liability for harm caused by a dug well. Digging on one’s own property does not incur liability, while digging in a public road or on land not owned by the person makes him liable for whatever falls into it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5341 - Zurah and Uthman ibn Isa narrated from Samaah, who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a man who digs a well in his house or on his land.
Imam (as) said: "If he digs it within his own property, there is no liability upon him. But if he digs it in a public road or in a place that does not belong to him, then he is liable for anything that falls into it."
